subject: Urban Planning
title: Variances and Special Permits
description: One-minute skill: Variances and Special Permits.

hook.text: If your project doesn't fit the zoning code, you can ask for a variance — a legal exception just for you.

buildup.text: Zoning boards hear variance requests at public hearings. Neighbors can object. The process takes months.

discovery.text: The variance system gives local boards enormous discretionary power. A project lives or dies on five people's vote.

twist.text: Connected developers get variances approved easily. Small builders without lawyers face rejection.

climax.text: Some cities are replacing variances with form-based codes — if your building fits the form, it's approved by right.

punchline.text: Zoning says no. The variance says maybe. Who you know says yes.

quiz.question: What is a zoning variance?
options: A permanent change to the city's zoning map for a whole district
A legal exception allowing a specific project to deviate from zoning rules
A fee paid to the city for building taller than the height limit
